hook: Lift a bowling ball onto a high shelf and nothing seems to happen, until it falls. Wind up a toy car and it sits still, until you let go. The energy is stored in the arrangement of interacting objects, ready to become motion. That stored energy is potential energy, and it belongs to a system, not to one object.

chain.cause: Two objects interact through a conservative force (gravity, an ideal spring)
chain.effect: the work the force does depends only on where the objects start and end

chain.cause: The work depends only on the configuration
chain.effect: the system can store energy in its configuration: potential energy, with ΔU = −W_conservative

chain.cause: The objects are pulled apart against gravity or a spring is squeezed
chain.effect: the system's potential energy increases: ΔU_g = mgΔy, U_s = ½k(Δx)²

chain.cause: Only changes in U appear in physics
chain.effect: the zero of potential energy can be placed wherever is convenient

chain.cause: A force does more work on a longer path, like kinetic friction
chain.effect: it is nonconservative and has no potential energy

ideas: Potential energy is energy stored in the configuration of a system of interacting objects. One object alone has none.
Near Earth: ΔU_g = mgΔy. For an ideal spring: U_s = ½k(Δx)², with Δx measured from the relaxed length.
A conservative force does work that depends only on the start and end positions; for it, W = −ΔU. Kinetic friction is nonconservative.
The zero of potential energy is a choice. Values change with the choice; changes do not.
Far from a planet: U_G = −Gm₁m₂/r, zero at infinite separation and negative everywhere else.

misconception.wrong: The book on the shelf has 29 J of potential energy.
misconception.right: The book-Earth system has 29 J of gravitational potential energy (with the floor as zero). The energy is stored in the interaction, so it belongs to the system.

summary: Potential energy is stored in the configuration of interacting objects and belongs to the system. ΔU_g = mgΔy near Earth, U_s = ½k(Δx)² for a spring, U_G = −Gm₁m₂/r far away. Only conservative forces have one; the zero is a free choice because only changes matter.
